source: Birmingham et al 1997 Lancet Epidemic Cholera in Burundi Great Rift Valley Lake Region
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 1970-01-01..1977-12-31. Source states: 'The pattern of transmission was similar to that in 1978, when the seventh pandemic first reached this region. Communities affected were limited to those near Lake Tanganyika and the Rusizi River. The river connects Lake Tanganyika with Lake Kivu to the north in Zaire and Rwanda.'. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: partial. PRE-INTRODUCTION ABSENCE. Rwanda is placed cholera-free for 1970-1977 not by an absence of reports but by the positive, well-documented fact that seventh-pandemic Vibrio cholerae had not yet reached the Great Rift Valley Lake region. Three independent lines of evidence agree: (1) Birmingham et al, Lancet 1997 - the seventh pandemic first reached this region in 1978, with the index cases at Rumonge on Lake Tanganyika in May 1978 in a household contact of a traveller from Tanzania, spreading north along the Rusizi River toward Lake Kivu in Zaire and Rwanda; (2) CDC EID 17(11) 2011 - cholera outbreaks have occurred in Burundi, Rwanda, DRC, Tanzania, Uganda and Kenya almost every year since 1977-1978, 'when the disease emerged in these countries'; (3) WHO GHO earliest-record test - the three Great Lakes countries Rwanda, Burundi and DRC all have 1978 as their first cholera record, whereas the countries to the east that were reached earlier by the pandemic do have pre-1978 records (Uganda from 1971, Kenya from 1971, Tanzania from 1974). That differential pattern is what true absence looks like; uniform non-reporting would not spare exactly the three landlocked Great Lakes countries. Rwanda entered the WHO reporting system with 838 cases in 1978, its first year of transmission. Surveillance capacity in 1970s Rwanda was limited, hence 'partial' and confidence 0.8 rather than higher. SINGLE ROW covering eight years - one piece of evidence, not eight; weight it accordingly and do not read 96 covered months as 96 independent observations.
